newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's BHF 9-mo profits up seven pct.
newsitem.headline: Germany's BHF 9-mo profits up seven pct.

text.p: BHF-Bank AG, Germany's seventh largest listed bank, said on Thursday operating profit in the first nine months of 1996 rose nearly seven percent.
Group operating profit after provisions rose 6.6 percent to 258 million marks ($170.6 million), the bank said in a statement. Net debt bad provisions were up 11.4 percent to 137 million marks.
BHF said it would be further tailoring its business structure with continued profit growth in mind.

Group net interest income rose 4.6 percent to 568 million marks, while net commission income was up by 4.7 percent to 333 million marks. Own-account trading profit was flat at 67 million marks, the bank said.
The figures mark a considerable improvement in earnings growth from the half-year, when BHF could only report a 3.5 percent gain in operating profit for the first six months.
The bank is currently seeking to concentrate on investment banking in a move away from its traditional lending business.
